q-105127.name: Question 1
q-105127.worked_solution:
The power set of $X,$ denoted $P(X),$ is the set that contains every possible subset of $X,$ including the empty set $∅.$

So, let's list all possible subsets of $X$ using a tree diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14180007/assets/bea8536b726a48046b995d180bd9136146d491721a9197f696c7a5e9af43a6ba.png)

According to our diagram, the subsets of $X$ are

$$
∅=\{\},\,\{x\},\,\{y\},\,\{x,y\}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
P(X)=\{∅,\{x\},\{y\},\{x,y\}\}.
$$

The power set of $Y,$ denoted $P(Y),$ is the set that contains every possible subset of $Y,$ including the empty set $∅.$

So, let's list out the subsets of $Y:$

- The subset with no elements is $∅.$

- The subset with $1$ element is $Y$ itself: $\{0\}.$

Therefore, we have

$$
